entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties' (OpenAI, dated October 7, 2026; the README notes it supersedes a September 23, 2026 version by updating one citation). Its main theorem (thm:main) takes an abelian variety A over Q̄ of dimension d with good reduction A_0 over F̄ₚ at a p-adic place w, a rational Hodge class γ in H^{2r}(A(C), Q(r)), and any Cartier divisors D_1,...,D_{d-r} on A_0. It shows that the traces of γ_0 against the divisor products are one rational number q in every ℓ-adic realization (ℓ ≠ p) and in crystalline cohomology. The corollary 'Algebraic specialization of rational Hodge classes' goes further: there is one rational algebraic cycle z_γ in CH^r(A_0)⊗Q, on the special fibre over F̄ₚ, whose ℓ-adic and crystalline cycle classes equal those of γ_0. Its proof transports γ to a CM abelian variety B by a quasi-isogeny of special fibres, and then uses the companion OpenAI manuscript 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (cited as OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1) to say that the CM class is algebraic.
entries.delivers: Algebraicity in characteristic p, for every residue characteristic p including 2, of the specializations at one fixed good-reduction place of rational Hodge classes on abelian varieties over Q̄, in every degree 2r. The cycles live on the reduction A_0 over F̄ₚ, not on A(C). The manuscript does not claim to settle the Hodge conjecture. It says the corollary 'neither asserts the Hodge conjecture for arbitrary abelian varieties in characteristic zero nor lifts z_γ to the original generic fiber'. The only characteristic-zero algebraicity it uses is the CM case from OpenAICMHodge2026, which this family does not prove. None of the statement about complex projective manifolds is addressed.
entries.remains: All of what the list asks: for every non-singular complex projective X, every rational Hodge class is a rational linear combination of classes of complex subvarieties. Left open even for abelian varieties: for a given rational Hodge class on A(C) the family produces no algebraic cycle on A(C), and it produces nothing in characteristic zero for non-CM abelian varieties or for any other variety.
entries.direction: proves algebraicity in characteristic p of specialized Hodge classes; the conjecture itself is not addressed
entries.conditional_on: The algebraic-specialization corollary depends on OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1 (the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, a companion OpenAI manuscript not read here). The main theorem's proof is stated to be independent of it. The construction also cites external results without proving them: Kisin–Zhou (2025, preprint), Pappas–Rapoport (2024), Gleason–Lim–Xu (Invent. Math. 2026, Corollary 6.3, for a uniformization condition), Milne (2009, Theorem 4.5), Deligne (1982), Blasius (1994) and Moonen (1998).
entries.doubts: (1) The abstract says every specialized Hodge class 'is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle' and does not say that the cycle lies on the reduction over F̄ₚ. The body makes that restriction and disclaims the characteristic-zero Hodge conjecture. (2) The algebraicity statement is an explicit additional input from the companion manuscript; the authors say the main theorem does not need it. (3) The text flags no step as sketched, but the proof is long and relies on several cited inputs that the authors state rather than prove.

entries.what_happened: Same manuscript, same corollary 'Algebraic specialization of rational Hodge classes'. For each rational Hodge class γ on A(C), with A over Q̄ abelian and good reduction at w, it produces z_γ in CH^r(A_0)⊗Q on the special fibre over F̄ₚ with cl_ℓ(z_γ) = γ_{0,ℓ} for every ℓ ≠ p. So the ℓ-adic realization of every specialized Hodge class lies in the image of the cycle map with Q coefficients. The manuscript does not state Tate's conjecture and does not discuss Galois invariance or descent to a finite field.
entries.delivers: Algebraicity over F̄ₚ of ℓ-adic classes that are specializations of rational Hodge classes on abelian varieties over Q̄ with good reduction at w. Tate's conjecture concerns Galois-invariant classes over finitely generated fields and asks that they be spanned by algebraic cycles. The family does not show that the classes it covers are Galois-invariant, does not show that the cycles can be taken over a finite field, and does not treat Tate's second conjecture. It therefore does not settle Tate's conjecture in any case as the list states it. At most it covers a restricted class of ℓ-adic classes, over an algebraic closure, and the manuscript does not present this as a case of Tate's conjecture.
entries.remains: Tate's first conjecture for smooth projective varieties over finitely generated fields in all codimensions, including divisors. Galois invariance and descent to finite fields for the classes the family covers. Tate's second conjecture. All varieties other than abelian varieties with good reduction at w over Q̄, and the strong (semisimplicity) form.
entries.direction: proves algebraicity over F̄ₚ of specialized Hodge classes; Tate's conjecture not addressed
entries.conditional_on: OpenAICMHodge2026, Theorem 1.1, as for the Hodge entry: the CM class κ is algebraic only by that companion result.
entries.doubts: The text does not show that the specialized ℓ-adic classes are Galois-invariant, which is the hypothesis Tate's conjecture needs. The cycle z_γ is built over F̄ₚ, and the text does not say it is defined over any finite field. Right after the fixed-theory corollary, the text says that result 'alone gives no algebraic cycle and proves neither the Hodge nor the Tate conjecture'. The algebraic-specialization corollary is a separate claim and is not discussed in those terms.

entries.not_relevant_because: The family proves that rational numbers obtained by pairing specialized Hodge classes with divisor products agree across ℓ-adic and crystalline realizations, and that those classes are algebraic over F̄ₚ. It neither states nor proves any of the four standard conjectures: algebraicity of the Lefschetz inverse, algebraicity of the Künneth projectors, equality of numerical and homological equivalence, or the sign in the Hodge standard conjecture. Its only Lefschetz input, that hard Lefschetz and its inverse restrict to divisor-generated subspaces, is cited from Milne (1999) as a known result.
